feasibility.title: Feasibility & Formulation
feasibility.card: Find out whether freeze-drying suits your product, and build a formulation that survives it.
feasibility.headline: Know if your product should be freeze-dried before you commit.
feasibility.lede: Small-scale screening runs and excipient studies tell you whether lyophilization improves stability, and which formulation gives the best cake.
caps: Liquid vs. lyo stability
Side-by-side stress studies compare your liquid product with freeze-dried samples so the decision rests on data.
Excipient screening
Bulking agents, cryoprotectants and buffers chosen to protect your active and form an elegant cake.
Fill and container selection
Fill depth, vial size and stopper design matched to drying time and reconstitution needs.
specBody: Screening runs on a laboratory freeze-dryer with product probes and cake imaging.
Results feed directly into thermal characterization and cycle development, with no transfer between teams.
spec: Sucrose, trehalose, mannitol, glycine and others
deliverables: Feasibility report with go / no-go recommendation

characterization.title: Thermal Characterization
characterization.card: Measure collapse and glass transition temperatures so the cycle is designed around facts, not guesses.
characterization.headline: Every cycle starts with the right temperatures.
characterization.lede: Freeze-dry microscopy and calorimetry find the critical temperatures your product must stay below during drying.
caps: Freeze-dry microscopy
We watch your formulation dry under a microscope and record the exact temperature where structure starts to fail.
Differential scanning calorimetry
Modulated DSC finds the glass transition of the frozen concentrate and any crystallizing components.
Frozen-state behavior
Annealing and nucleation studies show how freezing conditions change ice structure and drying speed.
specBody: Characterization usually takes one to two weeks and needs only a few milliliters of product.
Results set the target product temperature, with a safety margin, for cycle development.

cycle-development.title: Cycle Development
cycle-development.card: Design and optimize a freeze-drying recipe that is short, robust and gentle on your product.
cycle-development.headline: Cycles built to be short, robust and repeatable.
cycle-development.lede: We write your first recipe from thermal data, then optimize primary drying so the cycle runs as fast as your product safely allows.
caps: First-pass recipe
Shelf temperature and chamber pressure set from your critical temperatures and heat-transfer data for the chosen vial.
Primary drying optimization
Product probes, pressure-rise tests and comparative pressure measurement show when drying ends, so no hours are wasted.
Design space mapping
We define the range of conditions that still give good product, which protects you when real equipment drifts.
specBody: Development runs on a pilot dryer that matches the controls and sensors of our production units.
Each run is documented so the final recipe is ready for a regulatory filing.
spec: Wireless product probes, Pirani vs. capacitance
deliverables: Cycle development report and final recipe
Run data for every development cycle

scale-up.title: Scale-up & Tech Transfer
scale-up.card: Move a cycle from pilot to production, or bring in a recipe developed somewhere else.
scale-up.headline: From pilot dryer to production, without surprises.
scale-up.lede: We characterize every dryer we own, so a recipe moves between scales with predictable results. We also take on cycles transferred from other sites.
caps: Equipment characterization
Vial heat transfer, shelf uniformity and condenser limits are measured for each dryer and kept on file.
Scale-up modeling
Models adjust your recipe for differences between pilot and production equipment before any product is used.
Inbound tech transfer
We review a recipe from another site, run engineering batches here and adjust before GMP manufacturing.
specBody: Engineering runs use placebo or product at full load to confirm drying times and moisture.
Transfer packages are written so they can be inspected by regulators.
deliverables: Scale-up or tech transfer protocol and report

gmp.title: GMP Freeze-Drying
gmp.card: Clinical and commercial lyophilization on production freeze-dryers with full process monitoring.
gmp.headline: GMP freeze-drying, from clinical lots to commercial supply.
gmp.lede: Production freeze-dryers with automatic loading run your validated recipe under GMP, with every sensor recorded in the batch record.
caps: Clinical batches
Small lots for Phase I to III on dryers that share controls with commercial units.
Commercial supply
Large production dryers with automatic loading and unloading systems for repeat batches.
Process validation
Process performance qualification and continued verification to support your license.
specBody: Dryers are steam sterilized and leak tested before each batch.
Every batch record includes the full cycle trend data, alarms and end-point evidence.
spec: Pilot 0.5 m², production 10 m² and 32 m²
deliverables: Executed GMP batch record with full cycle data

testing.title: Release Testing
testing.card: Moisture, reconstitution, cake appearance and stability testing for lyophilized product.
testing.headline: Testing designed for freeze-dried products.
testing.lede: Our lab runs the tests a lyophilized product needs for release and stability, so results come back quickly from the same site.
caps: Residual moisture
Coulometric Karl Fischer and non-destructive NIR, including edge and center vial comparison.
Cake and reconstitution
Cake appearance grading, reconstitution time and solution clarity against your specification.
Stability programs
ICH long-term and accelerated storage with scheduled pulls and trend reporting.
specBody: Methods are validated or transferred to support release and regulatory filings.
Certificates of analysis are issued by the same QA unit that releases the batch.
